subtitle: select(), filter(), withColumn(), and handling real nulls.

eyebrow: Reading both real files this dataset ships with
code:
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("TaxiTransform").getOrCreate()

trips = spark.read.parquet("/data/nyc_taxi/yellow_tripdata_2024-01.parquet")
zones = spark.read.csv("/data/nyc_taxi/taxi_zone_lookup.csv", header=True, inferSchema=True)

zones.show(5)
caption: header=True treats row one as column names; inferSchema=True has Spark guess real types instead of defaulting to strings.

code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

fares = trips.select("VendorID", "passenger_count", "trip_distance", "fare_amount")

valid_fares = fares.filter(col("fare_amount") > 0)
long_trips = fares.filter((col("trip_distance") > 10) & (col("passenger_count") >= 1))
caption: select() narrows to the columns you need. Combining filter conditions needs & and |, not Python's and/or.

eyebrow: Why col() instead of a plain Python comparison
code:
# Works, but fragile with compound conditions:
trips.filter(trips.fare_amount > 0)

# More common, more flexible:
trips.filter(col("fare_amount") > 0)
caption: col() isn't tied to one DataFrame variable — essential once you're combining columns from two DataFrames, as in Lesson 46's joins.

eyebrow: withColumn() — adding or replacing a column
code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import round as spark_round

trips = trips.withColumn("fare_per_mile", spark_round(col("fare_amount") / col("trip_distance"), 2))
trips.select("trip_distance", "fare_amount", "fare_per_mile").show(5)
caption: withColumn() replaces a column if the name exists, or adds a new one if it doesn't — the real shape of most transform logic.
na.drop() removes rows missing a required field; na.fill() substitutes a reasonable default instead.
